high_consensus.description: Critical and highly actionable. If auth assumptions are wrong, Sprint 1 cannot deliver. A Sprint 0 spike with a go/no-go gate is proportionate and directly de-risks the core architecture.

Strong security gap identification. Redaction cannot rely on an unknown key format, and proposing value-based fallback is practical. Clear acceptance criteria can be added with low-to-moderate effort.

High-value reliability improvement. Bedrock-specific error taxonomy materially affects retries and circuit-breaker behavior; without this, availability handling will be wrong. Concrete and domain-appropriate.

Critical for model availability. Cross-region inference profiles are a real Bedrock constraint for newer Anthropic models, so treating this as future work risks day-1 failure. Very strong and actionable.
Good policy/UX gap to close. Fallback behavior with dual credentials has real cost and compliance implications. Worth adding, though somewhat product-policy dependent rather than purely technical.

disputed.description: Excellent catch and likely blocker. Colon-containing Bedrock model IDs can break provider:model parsing unless explicitly defined and tested. Concrete acceptance criteria are necessary and high ROI.

Important compatibility verification. Declared support for thinking traces without Bedrock parity proof is risky for downstream workflows. Adding explicit parity tests/fallback behavior is appropriate.

blockers.concern: API contract uncertainty is deferred too late (model IDs, Converse parity, endpoint semantics are placeholders/TBD)
blockers.why_matters: Multiple FRs rely on unverified Bedrock specifics; if even one is incorrect (Converse feature parity, model naming, token usage fields), adapter and config design may break late in sprint.
blockers.location: FR-2 implementation guidance, FR-5 Day 1 model coverage, Assumptions A2/A4
blockers.recommendation: Create a mandatory 'Contract Verification Spike' milestone before Sprint 1 acceptance starts, and block implementation until endpoint, payloads, and response normalization are proven.

blockers.concern: Bedrock API Keys may not be the auth modality users actually need
blockers.why_matters: Assumption A1 is load-bearing for the entire v1 scope. The user explicitly said 'i am not sure how bedrock works' and deferred to the team. Most enterprise AWS customers use IAM roles, not the relatively new Bedrock API Keys feature. If the actual user need is SigV4/IAM, v1 ships and is unusable for the requesting customer, forcing immediate v2 work and wasted Sprint 1 effort.
blockers.recommendation: Before /architect, directly confirm with the requesting Bedrock users (not just the issue reporter) whether they have/use Bedrock API Keys vs IAM credentials. A 5-minute survey saves a sprint. Consider building SigV4 first if survey shows IAM dominance.

blockers.concern: Bedrock Converse API feature parity with direct Anthropic is unverified
blockers.why_matters: FR-2 assumes Converse supports thinking_traces, tools, function_calling, and Anthropic-specific extended thinking. Historically Bedrock Converse has lagged direct Anthropic by weeks-to-months on new features (e.g., extended thinking, prompt caching, computer use). If Converse lacks thinking_traces for Opus 4.7, G-4 (Bedrock-Anthropic as drop-in replacement) fails and Flatline workflows that depend on thinking traces silently degrade.
blockers.location: FR-2, FR-5, Assumption A2, Risk R-3
blockers.recommendation: Add a Sprint 0 spike to verify Converse capability matrix against Loa's actual Anthropic feature usage. Document explicit feature-gap fallback to InvokeModel before any code lands. Make api_format per-capability, not per-model.

blockers.concern: Core auth assumption may be wrong: v1 depends on Bedrock API Keys + Bearer flow that may not be universally available or sufficient for target users
blockers.why_matters: If customer environments actually require IAM/SigV4 (common in enterprise AWS), the shipped v1 path will be unusable, forcing redesign and missing the primary adoption goal.
blockers.location: Assumptions A1, FR-3, FR-4, Executive Summary (v1 vs v2 split)
blockers.recommendation: Add a hard pre-build validation gate with real customer accounts: confirm auth modality, endpoint/header contract, and org policy compatibility before Sprint 1 coding.

blockers.concern: Fallback policy can violate user compliance intent by silently routing Bedrock users to direct Anthropic
blockers.why_matters: NFR-R1 proposes Bedrock -> Anthropic fallback, which may breach residency/compliance constraints for users who chose Bedrock to avoid direct vendor egress.
blockers.location: NFR-R1 fallback extension, Problem Statement (data plane/compliance motivation)
blockers.recommendation: Make cross-provider fallback opt-in per model/provider with explicit compliance flag; default to fail-closed for Bedrock-configured compliance profiles.

blockers.concern: Security requirements are incomplete: no explicit key rotation, revocation, or incident response flow for AWS_BEDROCK_API_KEY
blockers.why_matters: Long-lived keys without rotation/revocation playbook increase blast radius and compliance risk; one leaked key can silently impact cost and data exposure.
blockers.recommendation: Add explicit non-functional requirements for key rotation cadence, revocation procedure, detection signals, and operational runbook ownership.
